productLossClosed: The shared Sidebar V2 card action slot now uses a real layout container instead of a text container, so nested action controls have valid Web DOM and stable Lynx hit testing.
The shared action slot stops tap propagation before the parent thread row can select the thread being deleted.
Lynx clears an active thread only after the typed delete command succeeds; command failures preserve the thread and surface through the existing error state.
All Lynx New Thread entry points still converge on one local draft per project and do not call the durable connector createThread command.
rootCause: The action area was rendered as HostText, producing a span around a button on Web and a text node around views on Lynx.
The nested close tap could continue to the parent row selection handler, making a successful delete look ineffective or unstable.
The previous delete path cleared active state before server acknowledgement and swallowed command failures at the Sidebar call site.
safetyBoundary: Automatic stale-shell recovery retains its 24-hour grace because external or older clients can still use create-then-start.
Only canonical untouched New thread shells receive the direct close affordance; threads with user messages, turns, sessions, approvals, pending input, or plans remain normal threads.
The verifier used a VACUUM snapshot and its own second disposable copy; live ~/.t3-lynxtron state was never opened for writing.
classification.evidenceBoundary: This checkpoint validates the exact Native pointer path for an automatically recovered stale shell, a manually deleted fresh canonical empty shell, and repeated local-draft creation. It does not claim a new fidelity-score reduction because the existing new-thread interaction/runtime cells were already at zero residual.
